description: A MineCraft utility mod for peer-to-peer multiplayer.  Allows users to play using worlds in synced directories (Google Drive for desktop, syncthing, network drives, etc.) by providing mutex locking for shared worlds.  No more waiting for the host to start the world, play your MP world whenever you want!

mods.name: SharedWorlds
mods.description: Take turns hosting one Minecraft world, kept in a shared or synced folder. Whoever opens it gets the latest copy; nobody else can host it until they quit.

releases.notes:
# SharedWorlds Playtest Guide (v0.1.0-alpha.1)

SharedWorlds lets a group take turns hosting one Minecraft world. The world lives in a shared folder: whoever opens it gets the latest copy, and nobody else can host it until they quit.

## Before you start

This is an early alpha. Expect bugs, and expect to lose progress at some point.

* **Back up any world you care about** before you start, and never test with your only copy of a world.
* The person running the test keeps a manual backup of the shared folder. Don't delete or rearrange anything in it.
* Only use the mod with the test world. Other worlds aren't affected, but there's no reason to take the risk.

## What you need

Everyone in the test must match these exactly. The mod doesn't check versions yet, so a mismatch can quietly damage the world.

|Item|Requirement|
|-|-|
|Minecraft|Java Edition 1.21.11|
|Mod loader|Fabric Loader 0.18.4 or newer|
|Fabric API|Required (any version for 1.21.11)|
|SharedWorlds|`sharedworlds-0.1.0-alpha.1.jar` from this release|
|Account|Your own real Minecraft account (no offline or cracked launchers)|
|Shared folder|A folder every player can reach: a network drive (best), or a synced folder (Syncthing, Google Drive for desktop)|
|Launcher|CurseForge app or Modrinth app (instructions for both below)|

## Install the mod

Make a separate profile just for the test, so your normal modpacks aren't touched.

### CurseForge app

1. Go to **Minecraft**, then **Create Custom Profile**.
2. Name it "SharedWorlds Test", choose version **1.21.11** and the **Fabric** loader, then create it.
3. Open the profile and add **Fabric API** through the normal mod search.
4. Click the profile's **⋯** menu, then **Open Folder**. Put `sharedworlds-0.1.0-alpha.1.jar` into the `mods` folder.

### Modrinth app

1. Create a new instance: version **1.21.11**, loader **Fabric**.
2. Add **Fabric API** from the content browser.
3. In the instance's content tab, use the option to add a mod from a file and choose `sharedworlds-0.1.0-alpha.1.jar`.

To check it worked, launch the profile and open **Singleplayer**: there should be a **Shared Worlds...** button next to the search box.

## Set up the shared world

One person shares the world; everyone else adds it. Both happen in game, from **Singleplayer → Shared Worlds...**, and there's nothing to edit by hand.

**If you're the one sharing it** (once):

1. Select the world in the list and click **Share "<world>"**.
2. Pick the shared folder. If it's empty, the world goes straight into it; otherwise a folder named after the world is created inside it.
3. Confirm. The last screen shows where the world ended up: tell everyone the location of that folder.

**If you're joining** (once per computer):

1. Make sure you can see the shared world's folder (the network drive is connected, or the sync has finished).
2. Click **Add from a shared folder...** and pick that world's folder.
3. Confirm. The world is copied into your worlds, with "(2)" added to its name if you already have one called that.

If you already have a copy of the world (for example, one copied by hand earlier), Add links it instead of copying it again.

Deleting a shared world from your world list deletes only your copy. The shared copy is never touched, and you can add it again any time.

## Playing

One person hosts at a time. Everyone else joins that person's game as usual.

* **To host:** open the world from Singleplayer as usual. The mod grabs the latest version from the shared folder and locks it so nobody else can host. Opening may pause for a few seconds while it copies; that's expected.
* **To join:** connect to the host the way you normally would (**e4mc/Essential/LAN**). Don't open the world yourself while someone else is hosting.
* **When you're done hosting:** quit to the title screen normally. The mod saves the world back to the shared folder during "Saving world", then releases the lock. Wait for that screen to finish.
